 By Mukul Kumar 
 Oct 20, 2026
 Jaiprakash Power Ventures Ltd. (NSE:JPPOWER) Q2 FY27: ₹511 Crore NARCL Settlement Cuts Profit to ₹33 Crore
 JPPOWER
 Source: Shutterstock

 Key Highlights 
 Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 stood at ₹1,512.12 crore.
 Net profit fell to ₹33.34 crore from ₹182.10 crore in Q2 FY26, a decline of about 82%.
 The quarter included an exceptional charge of about ₹511 crore related to a debt settlement with NARCL.
 The statutory auditors issued a qualified opinion relating to a ₹5,696.51 crore recompense claim by lenders, which the company disputes.
 Q1 FY27 net profit had been ₹468.84 crore, highlighting the sharp sequential swing.
 Jaiprakash Power Ventures Ltd. (NSE:JPPOWER) reported a steep decline in September-quarter profit as a one-time settlement with the National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd (NARCL) overshadowed steady operations. The Board met on October 19, 2026 to approve the unaudited standalone and consolidated results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026.
 Beyond the headline numbers, the results disclosure brings legal and governance matters into focus, making this a quarter where the notes to accounts are as important as the profit and loss statement.
 Revenue and Profitability Performance 
 Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was ₹1,512.12 crore, modestly higher than the year-ago quarter, indicating that the company’s thermal and hydro generation businesses continued to operate at a broadly stable level. For context, total income in Q2 FY26 was ₹1,478.49 crore.
 Net profit, however, fell to ₹33.34 crore from ₹182.10 crore in Q2 FY26. The sequential comparison is starker: in Q1 FY27, the company reported net profit of ₹468.84 crore. The main reason for the decline is an exceptional charge of about ₹511 crore recognised for the settlement of NARCL’s claim. Excluding this one-time item, the underlying profitability of the business would have been considerably higher than the reported figure.
 The NARCL Settlement 
 NARCL, the government-backed asset reconstruction company, acquires stressed loans from banks. Jaiprakash Power has settled a claim related to insolvency proceedings for about ₹511 crore, which has been charged as an exceptional item. While the charge reduces reported profit for the quarter, settlements of this nature can remove uncertainty and potential legal overhangs, provided they result in a full and final resolution.
 Auditor Qualification and Lender Claims 
 A more significant concern for investors is the statutory auditors’ qualified opinion relating to a recompense claim of ₹5,696.51 crore raised by lenders. Recompense clauses typically allow lenders to recover concessions granted during a debt restructuring once a borrower’s financial position improves. The company disputes the claim and has not provided for it in its accounts.
 Given its size relative to the company’s quarterly earnings, the outcome of this dispute could materially affect the balance sheet. A qualified audit opinion signals that the auditors could not fully agree with the accounting treatment, and investors generally treat such qualifications as an important risk factor.
 Other Developments 
 The results period was also marked by changes in senior management and continuing legal matters, including issues related to sand mining. Earlier in the year, there were disclosures regarding the pledge of the company’s shares by a significant shareholder. Together, these developments suggest that corporate and legal developments will remain a key driver of sentiment alongside operational performance.
 Key Risks 
 Key risks include the outcome of the ₹5,696.51 crore lender recompense claim, any further exceptional charges from legacy disputes, regulatory and legal proceedings, fuel cost and power tariff movements, and the execution of management transitions. Volatility in merchant power prices can also affect earnings for generators with uncontracted capacity.
 What Investors Should Watch 
 Investors will look for clarity on the legal status of the recompense claim, confirmation that the NARCL settlement fully resolves the related proceedings, updates on management changes and operational metrics such as plant load factors and realisations. The removal or persistence of the auditor qualification in future results will be a key indicator.
 Conclusion 
 Jaiprakash Power Ventures’ Q2 FY27 profit decline to ₹33.34 crore was driven mainly by a ₹511 crore exceptional settlement with NARCL, while revenue remained stable at ₹1,512.12 crore. The larger issue is the auditors’ qualification on a ₹5,696.51 crore lender claim, which adds uncertainty to the balance sheet. Operational stability offers some support, but the resolution of legacy liabilities will likely determine the company’s near-term trajectory.
 FAQs 
 Q: What was Jaiprakash Power’s Q2 FY27 net profit? 
 A: Net profit was ₹33.34 crore, down from ₹182.10 crore in Q2 FY26.
 Q: Why did profit decline? 
 A: Mainly due to an exceptional charge of about ₹511 crore related to a debt settlement with NARCL.
 Q: What is the auditor qualification about? 
 A: It relates to a ₹5,696.51 crore recompense claim by lenders, which the company disputes and has not provided for.
 Q: What was the company’s Q2 FY27 revenue? 
 A: Revenue from operations was ₹1,512.12 crore.
